experimental_conditions.statistics: two-way ANOVA for polyfunctionality; paired T-tests for individual markers

data.applicable_scenario: GUCY2C-targeted CAR-T cell therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (solid tumor)

outcomes.cytokine_release: Statistically significant improvement over the CD28HTM CAR in the fraction of cells producing at least one inflammatory cytokine after antigen stimulation, in both CD8+ (p = .048) and CD4+ (p = .0005) T cells, although overall inflammatory cytokine production with this CAR is not robust. Within the total CD8+ population TNFɑ production was similar between the two CARs, while there were more IL-2 and IFNɣ producing CD8HTM CAR-T cells. In the CD4+ population there was a statistically significant increase in the percentage of cells producing each of the three inflammatory cytokines. Polyfunctionality (the fractions producing one, two or three cytokines and the specific TNFɑ/IFNɣ/IL-2 combinations) was equivalent between the two CARs.
outcomes.granzyme_b: CD8+ CD8HTM CAR-T cells produced significantly more granzyme B after antigen stimulation than CD28HTM CAR-T cells; a statistically significant increase was also observed in CD4+ CD8HTM CAR-T cells, although less robust than in CD8+ cells. Both CARs had equivalent granzyme B+ percentages with control peptide stimulation.
